headline: The falling hazard in agent time-horizon curves is between-task frailty, not within-task degradation: hold the task fixed and the per-minute hazard is flat.
current_belief: Hamilton (Jan 2026) fits a pooled Weibull with shape about 0.6 for frontier agents and reads it as the agents' hazard; Ord 2505.05115 reads a half-life; METR's own logistic-in-log-time curve is the sigma^2 = 1 gamma-frailty curve without being named as one (X-2026-W42-S7F9, derivation in the seed record)
if_true: Horizon producers publish the frailty variance or the within-task run agreement beside every 50% and 80% horizon and label the 80% horizon a share of tasks within reach; forecasters use k_cond for single-task tails and sigma^2 for reach; pass^k reporters replace one per-step reliability with a per-task distribution
if_false: The within-task hazard falls too (k_cond well below 1): agents do degrade along a task, which makes the horizon curve a property of agents after all and makes the step-clock hazard shape (S7xF9) the next question
probes: X-2026-W42-S7F9 (frailty refit of METR-Horizon-v1.1 runs; $0, 3 d; no scorecard)
import:2026-W43-S7xF9 (step-clock hazard on tau-bench; ~$300-600 + 60 GPU-h; no scorecard)

headline: Most published real-to-sim validity claims rest on policy pairs their own real-world sample cannot resolve.
current_belief: Real-to-sim papers report rank agreement as point estimates over a handful of pairs (YUBI 2610.17521: 9 pairs, no interval; PhAIL 2605.29710 on cohort sizes); YUBI IV: its Wilson intervals 'are not confidence intervals for ranking accuracy or tests of the difference between policies'; 2606.10366 4.1: '5 real-world rollouts for each policy, task, and perturbation dimension'; Kaedim 2610.00731 App. B: 'We do not report MMRV on this basis'
if_true: Real-to-sim validation papers report resolvable fraction and chance-corrected agreement; benchmark owners publish the sample-size table
if_false: Rank agreement is robust even on unresolvable pairs — then the field's practice is fine and the note says so
probes: C-W43-13 (killed by red team 2026-10-20; the probe's zero-cost step was run on three tables and the pre-registered kill fired)
